questions.stem: A box plot displays five key values. Which of these is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: A box plot shows the minimum, lower quartile ($Q_1$), median ($Q_2$), upper quartile ($Q_3$), and maximum. The mean is not shown.

questions.stem: The 'box' in a box plot represents:

options.text: The middle 50% of the data (from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$)

questions.explanation: The box spans from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$, representing the interquartile range -- the middle 50% of the data.

questions.stem: A box plot has $Q_1 = 25$, $Q_2 = 35$, $Q_3 = 50$. What is the IQR?
If the median line in a box plot is closer to $Q_1$ than $Q_3$, this suggests the data is:
questions.explanation: When the median is closer to $Q_1$, there is more data spread above the median, indicating positive (right) skew.

questions.stem: Two box plots are drawn on the same scale. Box plot A has a wider box than box plot B. This means:

options.text: Dataset A has a larger IQR (more spread in the middle 50%)
Dataset A has a larger range
Dataset A has a higher median
Dataset A has more data items

questions.explanation: The width of the box represents the IQR. A wider box means a larger IQR, indicating more spread in the central 50% of the data.

questions.stem: The 'whiskers' of a box plot extend from:

options.text: $Q_1$ to the minimum and $Q_3$ to the maximum

questions.explanation: The whiskers extend from $Q_1$ down to the minimum value and from $Q_3$ up to the maximum value.
